chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Circular breathing makes Haitian headlines
summary: Budd's five-minute held note astonishes Haitians, and he explains circular breathing, as Clark Terry and Buster Bailey also did.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: And I never will forget, I was written up in every Haitian newspaper, front page news, because I used the circular breathing thing, and I held a note for about five minutes, and they wanted to know what God did I have in New York that could give me all of this breath, you know.
Explain that if you can, Budd, because I think you and Clark Terry and Buster Bailey --
Clark was a master and Buster was a --
And Buster would be in there and Clark Kerry, one of the few people that know about this circular breathing.

Yeah, it's a hard thing to explain. It isn't too hard to explain. It's just hard to learn how to do, but all of a sudden one day it comes to you. Now you know you say -- you know how you could be talking with somebody, and they would disagree with you, and they'd say, oh, p-f-f-f-t, you know.

Like -- well, this is the thing. You fill up your jaw, and you say p-f-f-f, like that, and while you're doing that, you intake air, like p-f-f-f. Now the thing is to keep it going smoothly. See, like p-f-f-f-f-f- --
See? And this is the trick. And, of course, you know, you must know breath control and how to put it into your instrument so you don't run out of breath so you have to break it.

And it just takes practice. But actually you fill up your jaws, and you poop it out, p-f-f-f, like that, and you breath at the same time, p-f-f-f, see? And this is what you call circular breathing. So they wrote me up in all the papers.
